## Context

See the [planning assignment](https://envs-193fe.github.io/assignments/08_interpretive-sign-plan.html) for an overview of this project, your goals, and basic expectations.

## Basic components

### Sign

[Your sign must be hand made and written.]{style="color: #D95204;"} Take this into account when you are designing the layout.

The final dimensions of your sign should be at least 8.5 × 14 inches (legal size), but can be larger.

Your sign should include:

- [ ] a title
- [ ] sections with text (500-600 words across all sections) explaining:
  - [ ] species or interaction(s) of interest, and why they are important to understand
  - [ ] why the field site and/or habitat of interest is important to conserve/protect
  - [ ] how humans historically interacted with the site or ecosystem
  - [ ] how humans currently interact with the site or ecosystem
- [ ] your own visuals, including at minimum (but not limited to): 
  - [ ] a depiction of the field site in a map, landscape, or cross-section
  - [ ] the species of interest
  
### Cited text

[This component may be typed.]{style="color: #D95204;"}

Most interpretive trail signs do not have citations. Yours shouldn't either! As part of your final submission, you will create a _separate document_ recreating the text on your sign with added citations.

Your cited text should include:

- [ ] the same text you present on your sign
- [ ] in-text citations
- [ ] a Works Cited or Reference page with
  - [ ] consistently formatted citations using one of the following options: 1) [American Psychological Association (APA)](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/apa_style/apa_style_introduction.html), 2) [Modern Language Association (MLA)](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/mla_style/mla_style_introduction.html), or 3) [Chicago Manual of Style](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/chicago_manual_18th_edition/cmos_formatting_and_style_guide/chicago_manual_of_style_18th_edition.html) format

Prior to citing your sources, you should verify that they are published articles, books, etc. For this assignment, you must _correctly_ cite at least:

- [ ] one original study (i.e. a work in which data are presented), and
- [ ] one book (e.g. a field guide, textbook, manual)

## Presentation

The presentation of information in your interpretive sign will be evaluated on:

- [ ] cohesion: all text and visuals have a cohesive look
- [ ] narrative: your writing depicts the species, site, and ecosystem accurately with evidence to support your claims, appropriate for the audience (visitors to the field site)
- [ ] written communication: your writing is clear, free of grammatical errors

## Creativity

As with your field guide, you can and should be creative in the way you present information for your interpretive sign. This component is reflective of your process in creating an interpretive sign for your field site of interest. Creativity will be evaluated on the novelty with which you have presented your work and the execution of your original vision. You will make a case for both these points in your self-evaluation.
